Q: Prevent lines and arrows from intersecting with each other A:

This is tricky - so this is a somehwat brittle solution you can start with. But using constraint = false on the edges leading to your external node, makes "... the edge not used in ranking the nodes" = it tells the engine to keep node-ranks regardless of these edges. I created an empty last row and connected nodes inside from left-to-right r7_a -> r7_b -> r7_c -> r7_d -> r7_e -> r7_f and with invisible edges to the 6-row-cells r6_a -> r7_a....

  • graph [splines=ortho] makes the edges follow 90-degree-turns and not splines.
  • If you had allowed splines, you could concentrate them

Limey's comment is relevant! If I had connected to external grid-item r7_c instead, then edges would cross:

comes close to the image you provided

Note: You have repeating code, so I'd suggest using functions + glue / sprintf / paste and an underlying color-matrix / label-matrix as input, this will make building the main-grid easier and more maintainable.

Q: What is a good way to find current route and render contents depending on it? A:

Solutions that React-Router provide are the use of layouts and nested routes. My question is not about how routing works, but how to make a conditional rendering exception in the layout or the parent of nested routes depending on the child route that is followed.

Q: Tensorflow Keras CV tutorials incorrectly working A:

After reviewing your code and the problem and also check the docs from TensorFlow it seems like you have an error in predicting_script.py because you are dividing by 255 manually, but your model already has Rescaling(1./255) as the first layer, i would changed it to something like this

img_array = np.array(img)
img_array = np.expand_dims(img_array, axis=0)

i also have to let you know that both files or projects are overwriting the same class_names.pkl, because flowers.py and fashion.py save to class_names.pkl in the same directory.

So one overwrites the other and your prediction script loads the wrong class names, so either keep them in separate directories or rename them, i did the code for that either

(Just make sure to update your prediction scripts to load the correct file accordingly)

#flowers.py
with open('flower_class_names.pkl', 'wb') as f:
    pickle.dump(class_names, f)

#fashion.py
with open('fashion_class_names.pkl', 'wb') as f:
    pickle.dump(class_names, f)

Finally, after searching a little bit deeper fashion MNIST will not work well with real photos because the model was trained on 28x28 grayscale images with white figures on black background.

Real photos of clothes look very different, so predictions will be unreliable and is basically a limitation of the dataset, not a bug in your code.
